HANDOFF PREPARED. HANDOFF — epic 061c (LLM provider seam), continuing a /rebar-implement run.

## Where to work
Worktree: /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam on branch feat/llm-provider-seam.
Second worktree /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-loadfix on fix/reconciler-module-identity holds ONLY the
unrelated CI fix (change 1050) — do not mix them.
Prefix every command with the worktree venv: env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" <cmd>

## Gerrit stack (six deep, NONE submitted; they land together when the epic closes)
  1048  9249  S7 Bedrock IAM + runbook        gates pending
  1043  2932  S3 Bedrock provider             LLM-Review +1, Verified -1  <-- BLOCKED
  1032  2682  runner.py split                 closed
  1023  dc0d  OpenAI-compatible endpoint      closed
  1014  f184  capabilities from ModelProfile  closed
  1012  7468  provider factory seam           closed
Separately: 1050 (bug 9f0b) sits on its OWN branch off origin/main, gates pending.

## THE IMMEDIATE TASK, in order
1. Wait for change 1050 to get LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1, then SUBMIT it to main.
2. In the provider-seam worktree: git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main
   (Change-Ids are in every commit, so 1043 and 1048 update in place on re-push.)
3. Re-push: git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main
4. 1043 should now go Verified +1. Then close S3:
   REBAR_GATE_REF=HEAD rebar transition 2932-8a98-6d70-4550 in_progress closed
5. Then close S7 (9249) the same way once 1048 is green. Its substantive work is DONE and verified in
   production; it only needs its gates.

## Why 1043 is red (do not re-diagnose from scratch)
A latent object-identity bug in reconciler TEST scaffolding, not in this epic's code. S3 only ADDED tests,
which changed xdist sharding and made it fire deterministically on macos/py3.13. Root cause and fix are
bug 9f0b-3d48-b935-428b / change 1050. It does NOT reproduce locally on py3.14 — CI is the reproducer.

## Then continue the epic
- S5 (343b, provenance) is next. BLOCKER ALREADY RECORDED ON ITS TICKET: providers.py is at 299 LOC
  against a <300 cap that is an ATTESTED criterion of closed story 7468. Its Scope targets that file.
  Three ranked options are in a ticket comment; recommendation is to put provenance assembly in
  capabilities.py (245 LOC, and it already owns the record provenance embeds).
- S6 (0d76, parity bar) is now genuinely runnable — see AWS below.
- S8 (eb6e, production cutover, NO fallback) then S9 (8625, ADR+docs, blocked behind S8).
  S9 blocked-behind-S8 is why the epic cannot close without the cutover.

## AWS — READ THIS BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT
Profile `frontier` NOW points at the PROJECT account 896586841071 / us-east-1 as user/joe_frontier,
which holds AdministratorAccess (I added it to the Admin group at the operator's request).
Earlier measurements in this run were taken in a DIFFERENT account (579718921998/us-east-2) and had to be
re-verified. Always confirm account+region before recording a measurement as fact.

Verified in the project account: on-demand model ids are NOT invokable (ValidationException, use inference
profiles); us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 CACHES (cache_write=4017 then cache_read=4017); us./global.
opus-4-5 silently do NOT cache while billing full input; us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 400s on temperature.

CRITICAL VERIFICATION RULE, learned the hard way twice: do NOT validate a scoped IAM grant from an
identity holding bedrock:* or AdministratorAccess — a wildcard cannot fail. And do NOT stop at
`aws iam simulate-principal-policy`: it answers what the policy permits for the action you NAMED, not
which action the service CHECKS. The Converse API authorizes against bedrock:InvokeModel, NOT
bedrock:Converse — the simulator said otherwise and was wrong; only a real call from the instance
(SSM, i-00880b2c7f13527c5) settled it. Full recipe: infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md.

## Gate mechanics that cost time in this run
- review-plan and the claim/close gates default to --ref origin/main, which PREDATES this unsubmitted
  stack, producing false "symbol does not exist" findings. Use `rebar review-plan <id> --ref HEAD` and
  `REBAR_GATE_REF=HEAD rebar claim/transition ...`. This is documented in --help; not knowing it cost
  several review rounds.
- The completion-verifier reads COMMITTED state. Uncommitted tests read as missing.
- Criteria whose evidence is external must be tagged [operator-attested] and cite a change id + vote, or
  the verifier cannot credit them.
- Do NOT mutate the working tree while a gating suite runs in it: conftest's pytest_sessionfinish
  escalates a clean run to exit 1 if git status gains entries (I tripped this by running terraform).
- Store lock contention with other sessions is normal; retry rather than force.

## Also filed this run (not part of 061c)
- 3147 (epic) + f161 (story E1): gate blindness to world-grounded evidence — forcing measurement
  provenance into [operator-attested] evidence. Advisory-first per ADR-0054, DET-first presence check.
- 9109 was closed by another session mid-run; I briefly edited that closed epic and reverted it.
